title: Bigfoot fever grips Damariscotta, but police say mystery solved

The hunt for Sasquatch in Damariscotta has officially come to an end.

The Damariscotta Police Department says reports of a possible Bigfoot sighting that sparked a wave of calls Monday turned out to be something far less legendary: a man wearing a costume.

Police said concerned and curious residents flooded the department with reports of a large, hairy figure roaming around town. Officer William Smith eventually tracked down the suspected Sasquatch on Main Street.

Instead of making an arrest, the officer stopped to chat with the costumed man, drawing a crowd of amused onlookers eager to snap photos with Damariscotta's most talked-about visitor.

After investigating the sighting, police found no evidence of criminal activity and, perhaps disappointingly for cryptid enthusiasts, no proof that the elusive Bigfoot had finally chosen Midcoast Maine as his home.

"We greatly appreciate everyone's excitement, curiosity, and willingness to keep an eye out for one another," Chief Erik Josephson wrote in a Facebook post. "While we didn't find Bigfoot, we did find something almost as rare: a town full of people willing to stop what they're doing to investigate a Bigfoot sighting."

The department has officially closed the case.
